method: Same selection system as live play: random subjects and formats, then random unseen questions. Recent subjects are avoided to keep the mix varied; first 100.

questions.prompt: Name a fictional pirate.
questions.scope: Named fictional sea, air and space pirates count, including characters who were pirates earlier in their story. A smuggler, sailor or marine is not automatically a pirate.

questions.prompt: Name an amusement park or theme-park resort.
questions.scope: Real parks and resort complexes count worldwide; familiar resort names would be accepted.

questions.prompt: Name one of the 88 official constellations.
questions.scope: Official IAU constellation names count. Recognized common names such as Capricorn and the Great Bear are accepted. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper are only parts of constellations.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with rock music.
Name a named pasta or noodle dish.
questions.scope: Named dishes and established menu preparations count, including familiar meal names such as spaghetti, udon and soba, filled pastas and gnocchi. A bare unfilled pasta-shape name without a dish or established menu preparation does not count. Plain tteokbokki is a rice-cake dish; rabokki includes noodles.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of shark or ray.
questions.scope: Established groups and species count; familiar common names would be accepted.

questions.prompt: Name a water sport or recreational activity on or in water.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a named weapon from a video game.
questions.scope: Unique named weapons and established weapon/item names count across all platforms.

questions.prompt: Name a government-issued currency, monetary unit or named historical coin.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name something people open using a key or a code.
questions.scope: Physical objects and devices count; the code can be a password or combination.

questions.prompt: Name a stringed musical instrument.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name an art or craft activity.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of animal that has a protective shell, carapace, bony plates or body armour.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a type of ball used in a sport, game or athletic training.
questions.scope: Named balls used in sports, games or athletic training count, including particular game-ball designs. Pucks, shuttlecocks and punching bags are not balls.

questions.prompt: Name a tea brand or tea company.
questions.scope: Real current or historical tea brands, tea companies and tea estates count. A tea variety, drink preparation or generic ingredient is not a company or brand. The inventory includes packaged-tea and ready-to-drink brands; owning a separate brand does not automatically make a generic parent-name guess eligible.

questions.prompt: Name a unit used to measure a physical quantity or digital information.
questions.scope: Established metric, customary, historical and scientific measurement units count, including named prefixed units. Currency units and arbitrary made-up units do not. Official unit symbols are accepted only when they name that actual unit.

questions.prompt: Name a type of tower.
questions.scope: Types of built tower count, including towers defined by their function or structure. Individual named towers do not.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Puzzle”.
Name a mystery TV or streaming show.
Name a kind of seal, sea lion or walrus.
questions.scope: Living and recently extinct species in the Mammal Diversity Database, plus established named animal groups, count. English names, documented scientific names and genuine public synonyms count. Prehistoric fossil-only species are outside this current-species inventory.

questions.prompt: Name an object that commonly has a hinge.
questions.scope: A common hinged version of the object must exist. Sliding or roll-up versions do not prevent a genuinely hinged object from counting.

questions.prompt: Name a named sandwich or established sandwich filling combination.
Name a piece of equipment used to take or process photographs.
questions.scope: Physical equipment, supplies and accessories used in still photography count, including darkroom materials. A finished photograph, filmed sequence or a device used only to mark a film take does not.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has won the NBA regular-season MVP award.
questions.scope: Winners of the main NBA regular-season Most Valuable Player award through the 2025–26 season count. Finals, All-Star and other leagues' MVP awards are different.

questions.prompt: Name a real named forest or woodland.
questions.scope: Real named forests, woodlands and established forest regions count, including national forests and named historical or petrified forests. A country or a fictional woodland does not count by itself.

questions.prompt: Name a Minecraft block you can strip, scrape or unwax by using an axe on it.
questions.scope: This asks for the right-click/use action. Merely chopping or breaking a block does not qualify. Both stripping wood and removing copper oxidation or wax count. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a type of flower.
questions.scope: Recognized common flower types and flowering plants grown for their blooms count, including named horticultural groups and documented varieties. Materials merely named after flowers, artificial flower products and unrelated decorative objects do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a song by The Weeknd.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to The Weeknd count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name an item or product used to wash, dry or care for laundry.
questions.scope: Laundry appliances, supplies, stain treatments and clothes-care tools count, as do named product types and established laundry-product brands, including historical ones. A garment itself is not a laundry supply.

questions.prompt: Name an art movement or recognized visual-art style.
questions.scope: Recognized visual-art movements, schools and historical styles count, including architectural and moving-image art movements. An individual artist, work, generic medium or music genre alone does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a weather event or weather condition.
questions.scope: Common and established technical names count; fictional weather does not.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the Minnesota Timberwolves.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not.

questions.prompt: Name a Legendary or Mythical Pokémon.
questions.scope: Species classified as Legendary or Mythical in the pinned PokéAPI data count. Forms share their species' answer identity. Pseudo-Legendary is a fan label and does not make a species Legendary.

questions.prompt: Name a river, lake, sea, ocean, gulf, bay or strait.
Name a record label or record company.
questions.scope: Real current and historical record labels, imprints and record companies count. A publisher, streaming platform or music store is not automatically a record label.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that can produce its own light.
questions.scope: Bioluminescence, including light produced by symbiotic bacteria in an animal's light organ, counts. Reflection, fluorescence and bright coloring alone do not. Broad animal groups count when they contain documented luminous members.

questions.prompt: Name a type of cookie or biscuit, including named branded varieties.
questions.scope: Named cookie and sweet biscuit varieties, brands and traditional preparations count. Regional names for the same biscuit share one answer; a cake or cracker is not automatically a cookie.

questions.prompt: Name a type of rock.
questions.scope: Recognized geological rock names, rock families and established natural stone varieties count. Common and scientific rock names are accepted. Individual minerals, chemical elements, whole mountains and manufactured building products are not rock types.

questions.prompt: Name an exercise that can be done using your bodyweight instead of added weights.
questions.scope: Named exercises and recognized variations count, including floor exercises, holds and movements on a pull-up bar. A bar or bench can provide support; dumbbells and loaded barbells are not required.

questions.prompt: Name an agent in Valorant.
questions.scope: Base-game and recorded expansion names count. Versions of the same named object count once.

questions.prompt: Name a piece of camping equipment.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a real, named bridge.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a music festival.
questions.scope: Named public music festivals anywhere in the world count; a one-off concert does not.

questions.prompt: Name an insect.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a character from the Harry Potter books or films.
questions.scope: Identifiable characters in the Harry Potter novels, films and their epilogues count, including creatures, ghosts and portraits. Real actors are not their fictional characters. Same-name characters share one answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name a mineral or other natural material used as a gemstone.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a driver who has competed in Formula One.
questions.scope: Drivers in the complete Jolpica/Ergast Formula One World Championship driver inventory count, including historical entrants and the Indianapolis 500 when it was part of that championship. A real surname can identify a valid driver; invented initials and racing three-letter codes do not count as names.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish commonly made with chicken.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a Pokémon Ability.
questions.scope: Named passive Pokémon Abilities from the core games and Pokémon Conquest count. Moves, types, held items and generic trainer actions are separate concepts.

questions.prompt: Name a color or a named shade.
questions.scope: Recognized English color names and published named shades count, including named pigments, Crayola colors and standard CSS color keywords. Regional spellings and ordinary synonyms share one answer. Patterns are not a single color. Different standard definitions of the same ordinary name do not create extra answers.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of swallow or martin.
questions.scope: Established named groups and species in the Hirundinidae bird family count, including recently extinct species. Common and scientific names are accepted. Real synonyms share an identity; unrelated birds and objects named after birds do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a desert.
questions.scope: Real named deserts and established desert regions worldwide count, including polar deserts and places traditionally known as deserts. A hotel, village, isolated rock, beach or generic dune does not automatically become a desert.

questions.prompt: Name a song with a color in its title.
questions.scope: Ordinary color words in released song titles count; color names used as surnames need context.

questions.prompt: Name a human muscle or muscle group.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has been on an NFL or AFL roster (1920–2026).
Name a move from a Pokémon video game.
questions.scope: Named moves from released Pokémon games count, including Z-Moves, Max Moves and Colosseum/XD Shadow moves. Physical/special implementations of the same named move share one answer. Generic actions and moves from fan games do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a type of chair or stool.
questions.scope: Recognizable chair and seated-stool designs count, past or present. Benches, couches, named individual thrones and the person chairing a meeting do not.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of primate. Named groups and species, living or extinct, count; a common or scientific name is accepted.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a type of custard or a dessert made with custard.
questions.scope: Named custards and desserts made using custard or custard powder count. A cream-only filling does not qualify merely because it is called cream.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Ariana Grande.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Ariana Grande count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name an action movie.
Name a landform, natural feature or kind of landscape.
Name an outfit from Fortnite.
questions.scope: Any recorded season or collaboration counts. These are cosmetic names, not Battle Royale weapon names.

questions.prompt: Name a team from the NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, WNBA or MLS.
questions.scope: Past and present teams from those six leagues count; familiar short team names would be accepted.

questions.prompt: Name a plant people eat.
questions.scope: Named edible plants count, including those eaten for fruit, leaves, roots or seeds; fungi are separate.

questions.prompt: Name an invention, tool or piece of technology.
Name a fast-food or fast-casual restaurant chain.
questions.scope: Real multi-location restaurant chains count worldwide; local independents do not.

questions.prompt: Name a musical genre or subgenre.
Name a type of boat, ship or other watercraft.
questions.scope: Kinds of boat, ship, raft or other vessel designed to travel on water or underwater count, past or present. Individual named vessels, wrecks, ice-only vehicles and descriptors of condition alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a flower or flowering block found in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Flower items and blocks count, including tall flowers and Nether-compatible flowers. Named crops and saplings do not become flowers merely because they are plants. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name an occupation or recognized job title.
Name a bird that cannot normally fly, including extinct flightless birds.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name someone who has played Major League Baseball (through 2025).
Name a character from Shrek or Puss in Boots.
questions.scope: Named or distinctly identified characters in the Shrek films and spin-offs, including Puss in Boots films, count. Identified groups such as the Three Little Pigs count. Voice actors and generic fairy-tale species alone do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a type of mechanical engine or motor.
questions.scope: Recognized mechanical prime movers and engine or motor types count, including combustion engines, turbines, rocket engines and electric, hydraulic or pneumatic motors. Electric generators, software engines and whole vehicles do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with pop music.
Name an edible shellfish or other edible aquatic invertebrate. Cephalopods count.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a playable hero in Dota 2.
questions.scope: The complete official playable hero roster in the October 25, 2026 snapshot counts. Items, cosmetics and non-playable creeps are not heroes.

questions.prompt: Name an object designed to be inflated.
questions.scope: Common inflatable objects and named inflatable equipment types count, whether filled with air, helium or another gas. Objects merely containing an empty cavity do not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a country made up entirely of islands.
questions.scope: Island countries and countries sharing an island count; Australia explicitly counts.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the New York Knicks.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that makes a regular seasonal migration.
questions.scope: Named species and animal groups with documented recurring seasonal, breeding or feeding migrations count, including migrating populations of a species. One-off escapes or an individual simply wandering do not.

questions.prompt: Name a musical instrument with a keyboard.
questions.scope: Recognized keyboard-instrument types and documented named keyboard instruments or models count. Keys and buttons form the musical playing interface; having ordinary valves or attaching an external controller does not automatically qualify another instrument.

questions.prompt: Name a sushi style or named sushi roll.
questions.scope: Established sushi preparations, named sushi rolls and recognizable filling-specific sushi varieties count. Sashimi by itself is not sushi because it lacks the seasoned rice. A fish or ingredient alone is not a prepared sushi variety.

questions.prompt: Name a chemical element used in everyday products.
questions.scope: There must be a documented consumer, industrial or medical use; exact product names are not required.

questions.prompt: Name something people can borrow from a public library.
questions.scope: Items must actually be offered by a public library somewhere; Library of Things collections count.

questions.prompt: Name a video game where you can drive a car or kart.
questions.scope: The driving must be part of the unmodded game, not a fan modification.

questions.prompt: Name a horror movie villain or monster.
questions.scope: Named villains, creatures and monster species from horror films count.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of animal that can regrow a lost body part.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a type of building or place used for worship.
questions.scope: Types of religious worship building or built shrine count across religions. Individual named landmarks and a minister or deity alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a combat sport or established martial art.
questions.scope: Named competitive fighting disciplines and established martial arts count, including forms practiced without full-contact competition. Fictional styles do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a structure or component found in a living cell.
questions.scope: Plant, animal, fungal and prokaryotic cell structures count. Whole organs or tissues are not structures inside one cell. Established molecular structures such as DNA and chromosomes count. Cellular structures and molecular assemblies count; an individual pigment such as chlorophyll is not an organelle or cell structure by itself.

questions.prompt: Name a food commonly cooked by frying.
questions.scope: Named foods and dishes count; a one-off experiment is not enough.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Space”.
Name a type of toy.
questions.scope: Recognized toy types and established named kinds of plaything count. Named branded toy kinds such as LEGO bricks, Barbie dolls or Play-Doh also count; a company name alone, a fictional character alone or an unrelated household object is not a toy type.

questions.prompt: Name a fictional robot.
questions.scope: Robots and droids from films, TV, books or games count; actors and real-world robots do not.

questions.prompt: Name a song by SZA.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to SZA count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name an athlete featured on a video game's cover or in its title.
questions.scope: An officially released sports game's cover athlete or title namesake qualifies.

questions.prompt: Name a real named dam.
questions.scope: Named real dams and barrages count, including historical dams and named projects already under construction. A reservoir name does not automatically name its dam, and fictional dams do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a food that is commonly pickled.
questions.scope: Vegetables, fruits, eggs, meats and seafood with established pickled preparations count. Vinegar and brine are ingredients, not foods being pickled.
